question.question:
Scenario-local loan policy. Loan balance in USD is 180000. Annual loan rate is 4.5 percent, simple interest. Horizon is 24 months. Available cash in USD is 50000. Prepayment at start in USD is 5000. Fee-free allowance is 15 percent of the balance; fee is 2 percent of only the prepayment above the allowance, else zero. The fee comes from cash, not the balance. Remaining cash sits in an offset account for the horizon, earning a credit at 4 percent per year, simple interest, months over 12. Loan interest is the post-prepayment balance times the loan rate times months over 12. The offset credit cannot exceed loan interest. Net cash cost is loan interest minus offset credit plus the fee. Report fee, loan interest, offset credit, and net cash cost.

Answer format: return only the exact numeric value interpreted in `usd`, using finite-decimal notation when it terminates in base 10 and an irreducible `numerator/denominator` fraction otherwise, with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: Report the prepayment fee charged on the amount above the allowance.
Report loan interest on the post-prepayment balance over the horizon.
Report the offset credit after applying the loan interest cap.
